clinician.trajectory_summary: A 2-year-old boy presented with sudden onset extremely painful bilateral non-pitting edema of both hands and purpuric lesions on the left cheek, nostril, and ear without fever or trauma (E001). Initial workup revealed normal blood cell count (excluding thrombocytopenia), elevated inflammatory markers (CRP 14.2 mg/dL, ESR 110 mm/hr), and negative urine analysis (excluding renal involvement) (E002). During observation, the edema and purpuric lesions spread to the arms, feet, and legs (E003). The patient received supportive treatment with ibuprofen only, and all lesions completely resolved within 72 hours (E005), consistent with the characteristic rapid spontaneous resolution of acute hemorrhagic edema of infancy.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Sudden onset extremely painful bilateral non-pitting edema of hands with facial purpuric lesions in a 2-year-old without fever or trauma
Normal blood cell count excluding thrombocytopenia and thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP)
Elevated inflammatory markers (CRP 14.2 mg/dL, ESR 110 mm/hr) consistent with inflammatory vasculitis
Negative urine analysis excluding renal involvement characteristic of Henoch-Schönlein purpura
Progression of edema and purpura to extremities during observation
Complete resolution within 72 hours with supportive care (ibuprofen) only, confirming the self-limited nature of the condition

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Normal blood cell count and platelet count documented (E002)
Age 2 years (younger than typical HSP), negative urine analysis excluding renal involvement (E002), and rapid 72-hour resolution (E005) inconsistent with HSP's typical prolonged course
Clinical presentation localized to skin and subcutaneous tissue with rapid spontaneous resolution rather than systemic bleeding or consumption coagulopathy
